description: Container Escape in Code Execution Environment Attackers could exploit container runtime vulnerabilities, misconfigured capabilities, or exposed system calls to break out of the container isolation and gain access to the host system or other containers. An attacker submits code that exploits a container runtime vulnerability to escape the container and access the underlying host system, potentially gaining access to other containers or AWS credentials.
references: recommendation: Implement strict container security controls
recommendation: Consider using AWS Firecracker microVMs

description: Unauthorized Code Execution Result Access Predictable or low-entropy execution IDs could allow attackers to guess valid IDs and access other users' execution results. Race conditions in result processing could lead to mixed results. An attacker monitors their own code execution results and attempts to guess or predict other users' execution IDs to access their results.

description: Resource Exhaustion via Code Execution Attackers could submit resource-intensive code that consumes maximum allowed resources or creates large amounts of data, causing service degradation. An attacker submits code that spawns multiple threads performing intensive calculations or generates large amounts of output data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Set up monitoring and alerting

description: API Gateway Security Bypass Attackers could bypass API security controls through missing CORS configurations, weak authentication, or CSRF vulnerabilities. An attacker creates a malicious website that makes cross-origin requests to the API endpoint, executing code without proper authorization.

Code Execution Process Escape Attackers could use system calls, library functions, or language features to execute commands outside the intended execution environment. An attacker submits code that uses Python's subprocess module or similar features to execute system commands.

description: Code Execution Orchestration Bottleneck Without proper queuing, multiple simultaneous code execution requests could overwhelm the system, leading to resource exhaustion or race conditions. An attacker sends many simultaneous code execution requests, overwhelming the orchestrator and preventing legitimate requests from being processed.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: Persistent Artifact Exposure Artifacts generated during code execution might persist beyond their intended lifetime, potentially exposing sensitive information or consuming storage resources. An attacker's code generates large artifacts that persist in storage, or examines artifacts left by previous executions.
